newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Monday in slow trade as profit-taking by retail investors dominated the market, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended an intraday low of 3,283 yuan ($396) per tonne, losing two yuan. It opened at 3,285 and hit a high of 3,288 yuan per tonne.
May fell 18 yuan to 3,297, July 38 to 3,300, November rose two to 3,396 and the January 1998 contract dropped six to 3,400 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 14,300 tonnes from 17,700 tonnes.
"Most investors have not returned from their holiday and this is the reason for such dull trade today," said one trader, referring to last week's four-day long Labour Day break.
"Retail investors were today's major force," he said.
"The surging stock markets are attracting a great deal of hot money away from the futures markets, which is another factor keeping things dull," another trader said.
Traders said soybeans were likely to consolidate around the current levels in the short term due to a lack of market-moving news. ($1=8.2947 yuan)
